label: Agent canvas mediator
info:
Validates what the Hermes agent publishes and republishes it into the panel's
namespace. This is the only thing that crosses that boundary.

  hermes/canvas/persistent  ->  wallpanel/canvas/persistent   (retained)
  hermes/canvas/ephemeral   ->  wallpanel/canvas/ephemeral    (retained)

ON IMPORT:
  1. Point ALL THREE mqtt nodes at one broker config authenticated as the
     'mediator' user. Per hermes-deploy/docs/todo-broker.md that user reads
     hermes/canvas and writes wallpanel/#, which is exactly this flow's job.

     A dedicated 'mediator' user is optional - existing admin credentials work
     and do not weaken anything, because what keeps the agent out of wallpanel/#
     is the ACL on the AGENT's credential, not this flow's. See
     kiosk-display/docs/agent-canvas-schema.md.

     Do NOT give this flow the 'hermes' credential, though. That is the agent's
     identity; a mediator holding it could publish as the agent, which defeats
     the point of validating what the agent publishes.
  2. Wire output 2 of the function node to the debug node if it is not already;
     a rejection that goes nowhere is a canvas that silently never appears.

An invalid payload is DROPPED, not forwarded, so the previously published
canvas stays up. An empty payload is forwarded, because that is how the agent
clears its own canvas.

The mqtt-out node has a blank topic and blank retain ON PURPOSE: it honours the
msg.topic and msg.retain the function node sets, so one output node serves both
canvases. If a Node-RED version defaults retain to 'false' instead of blank, the
panel will render on a live publish and then show nothing after a reboot - check
that first.

Contract: kiosk-display/docs/agent-canvas-schema.md (canonical).

name: validate against the v1 schema
